questions.q: At a weekly haat in Hyderabad, Gopal buys turmeric powder in three sacks of 2450 g each and one sack of 500 g. He can pack it all into 10 equal tins, selling each tin at ₹120, or into 100 equal pouches, selling each pouch at ₹14 but spending ₹3 on packing material for every pouch. (a) Find the total turmeric in kilograms. (b) How many kilograms go into each tin? (c) How many grams go into each pouch? (d) Which packing should Gopal choose to earn more? Support your choice with figures.
questions.a: (a) 3 × 2450 + 500 = 7850 g = 7.85 kg. (b) 0.785 kg. (c) 78.5 g. (d) Tins give ₹1200. Pouches give ₹1400 less ₹300 packing = ₹1100. Tins earn ₹100 more, so choose tins (pouches only win if packing cost is under ₹2 each).
s: Part (a): adds 3 × 2450 + 500 = 7850 g and writes 7.85 kg
Part (d): compares net ₹1200 with ₹1100 and recommends tins

questions.q: A bakery's 1000 identical biscuits together weigh 12.5 kg. (a) Find the weight of one biscuit in grams. (b) Find the weight, in kilograms, of a pack of 24 such biscuits.
s: Part (a): divides 12.5 kg by 1000 and converts 0.0125 kg to 12.5 g
Part (b): multiplies the single-biscuit weight by 24 to get 0.3 kg

Third division with a different divisor checked

Kabir measures a pencil as 0.142 m. Arun, measuring the same pencil, writes 1.42 cm. (a) Express 0.142 m in centimetres and in millimetres. (b) Say what Arun did wrong.
questions.a: (a) 0.142 × 100 = 14.2 cm and 0.142 × 1000 = 142 mm. (b) Arun divided by 100 (moving the point two places left) instead of multiplying by 100.
s: Part (b): identifies that he moved the point the wrong way (divided instead of multiplied)

questions.q: Meena wants to divide 7.8 by 100 and then multiply the result by 1000. She writes 7.8 ÷ 100 = 0.78 and 0.78 × 1000 = 780. (a) Find the step where she goes wrong and correct it. (b) Write her correct final answer and say which single operation on 7.8 gives the same result.
questions.a: (a) The first step is wrong: 7.8 ÷ 100 = 0.078, not 0.78. (b) 0.078 × 1000 = 78, the same as 7.8 × 10.
s: Part (b): gets 78 and links it to 7.8 × 10

questions.q: Rohit repeatedly divides 3.07 by 10. (a) Write the first four results. (b) Describe how the number of digits after the point changes at each division. (c) Without dividing, say how many digits after the point 3.07 ÷ 1000000 has and write it. (d) A number divided by 1000 gives 0.00307; find the number.
questions.a: (a) 0.307, 0.0307, 0.00307, 0.000307. (b) Each division by 10 adds one digit after the point; 3.07 has 2 and after n divisions there are 2 + n. (c) 2 + 6 = 8 digits: 0.00000307. (d) 0.00307 × 1000 = 3.07.
s: Part (b): one more digit after the point per division
Part (d): reverses the division to get 3.07

questions.q: Which of these is NOT equal to 0.372?

Canteen A in a school at Pune shares 25 kg of rice equally into 1000 portions. Canteen B shares 3.1 kg of rice equally into 100 portions. (a) Find the rice in one portion of A, in kg and in g. (b) Find the same for B. (c) Find how much more one B portion is, in grams. (d) Which canteen gives the smaller portion, and how many kilograms of rice does it save over 10000 students compared with the other?
questions.a: (a) 0.025 kg = 25 g. (b) 0.031 kg = 31 g. (c) 6 g = 0.006 kg. (d) Canteen A gives the smaller portion; over 10000 students it uses 0.006 × 10000 = 60 kg less.
s: Part (d): names canteen A and finds 60 kg saved

questions.q: The office of a school in Mysuru measures that a pile of 1000 sheets of paper is 95 mm high. It needs 10000 sheets for the annual day programme, but the cupboard shelf gap is only 90 cm. Option A is to buy all 10000 sheets in one lot at ₹0.42 a sheet and pay ₹350 to raise the shelf. Option B is to buy two lots of 5000 sheets at ₹0.45 a sheet, which fit as two piles. (a) Find the thickness of one sheet in millimetres. (b) Find the height of 100 sheets in centimetres. (c) Find the height of 10000 sheets in centimetres. (d) Which option costs less, and is the lower cost the only thing to weigh? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) 0.095 mm. (b) 0.95 cm. (c) 95 cm, more than the 90 cm gap. (d) A costs 4200 + 350 = ₹4550; B costs ₹4500. B is ₹50 cheaper and needs no change to the shelf; A is better only if the price might rise or lots are hard to get again.
s: Part (c): 0.095 × 10000 = 950 mm = 95 cm, more than 90 cm
Part (d): compares ₹4550 with ₹4500 and justifies the choice with a further consideration

questions.q: Meera writes 7/10 + 3/1000 as 0.73. (a) Write the correct decimal. (b) By how much, as a decimal, is Meera's number larger than the correct one?
s: Part (a): puts 3 in the thousandths place to get 0.703

questions.q:
Match each calculation in Column I with its value in Column II.
Column I: 1. 0.0417 × 100  2. 41.7 ÷ 1000  3. 4.17 × 10  4. 0.417 ÷ 100
Column II: a. 0.00417  b. 0.0417  c. 41.7  d. 4.17
Rohan says, "3.725 ÷ 100 = 0.3725, because the decimal point moves one place to the left." Do you agree? Check by writing the division as a fraction and give the correct value.
questions.a: No. 3.725 = 3725/1000, so 3.725 ÷ 100 = 3725/100000 = 0.03725. Dividing by 100 moves the point two places left (one place is for dividing by 10), and a zero fills the ones place.
s: Gives the verdict that Rohan is not right
Explains that two places, not one, are needed and a zero fills the ones place

questions.q:
Given that 36 × 25 = 900, match each product in Column I with its value in Column II.
Column I: 1. 3.6 × 2.5  2. 0.036 × 0.25  3. 3.6 × 0.025  4. 360 × 0.25
Column II: a. 0.09  b. 90  c. 9  d. 0.009

Oranges cost ₹84.50 per kg. Bhavna buys 1.250 kg. (a) Find the price by multiplying 84.50 × 1.250 as 8450 × 1250 and placing the point. (b) Find 84.5 × 1.25 and compare. (c) Does it matter that we dropped the zeroes? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 8450 × 1250 = 10562500, with 2 + 3 = 5 places gives 105.625. (b) 845 × 125 = 105625, 1 + 2 = 3 places gives 105.625. Same. (c) No: 84.50 = 84.5 and 1.250 = 1.25 are equal numbers, so the product is the same; the extra zeroes only add decimal places that the product also has as zeroes.
s: Part (a): multiplies 8450 × 1250 and places 5 decimal places to get 105.625
Part (b): multiplies 845 × 125 with 3 places and gets the same 105.625
Part (c): explains that trailing zeroes do not change the value of the factors

questions.q: Kavya buys 3 pens at ₹9.5 each and 2 rulers at ₹6.25 each from the school shop. How much does she pay?
(a) Before any final zero is dropped, how many digits after the decimal point does the product 0.045 × 0.8 have? (b) Find the product and write it without the final zero.
questions.a: (a) 45 × 8 = 360 and 3 + 1 = 4 digits after the point, so the product is 0.0360. (b) Dropping the final zero gives 0.036.
s: Part (a): finds 4 places by adding 3 and 1
Part (b): 45 × 8 = 360, placed as 0.0360 and written as 0.036

questions.q: A school in Chennai plans a picnic for 40 students to a fort 110 km away. Bus A runs 8.4 km on each litre of diesel and Bus B runs 9.6 km on each litre; each has a full 12.5-litre tank. Bus B's hire is ₹3650 and Bus A's is ₹3200, so B costs ₹11.25 more for each of the 40 students; the parents have agreed to pay at most ₹10 more per student than the Bus A plan. (a) How far can Bus A go on a full tank? (b) How far can Bus B go? (c) Find the total extra the parents will pay at most, the total extra B's hire needs at ₹11.25 a student, and the shortfall. (d) Which bus should the school hire, if the only fuel pump on the route is 90 km from the school? Give a reason with figures.
questions.a: (a) 8.4 × 12.5 = 105 km. (b) 9.6 × 12.5 = 120 km. (c) Parents' cap 10 × 40 = ₹400; B's extra 11.25 × 40 = ₹450; shortfall ₹50. (d) Bus A can reach the pump at 90 km (it can run 105 km) and refuel, so it fits the parents' cap with no school money. Bus B reaches the fort without a stop but needs ₹50 from the school fund. A sound answer picks either and states these figures; hiring A with a planned stop at the 90 km pump costs nothing extra, hiring B is justified only if the school will pay the ₹50 for the saved stop.
s: Part (d): decision using the 90 km pump (within 105 km) and the ₹50 shortfall

questions.q: Isha says 0.6 × 0.7 = 4.2 because 6 × 7 = 42, while Sheena says it is 0.42. Write 0.6 and 0.7 as fractions and multiply them to decide who is right, and say how many digits after the point the product must have.
questions.a: Sheena is right. 6/10 × 7/10 = 42/100 = 0.42, which has 1 + 1 = 2 digits after the point; Isha placed the point wrongly.
s: Names Sheena and links 2 places to the 10 × 10 denominator

questions.q: For the annual day, a school in Surat needs a carpet for a rectangular stage 7.5 m long and 4.8 m wide. Vendor A sells carpet cut to size at ₹85.50 per square metre and charges ₹150 for fitting. Vendor B sells it only in whole pieces of 40 square metres at ₹80.75 per square metre, with free fitting. (a) Find the area of the stage. (b) Find Vendor A's total bill including fitting. (c) Find Vendor B's bill. (d) Which vendor should the school choose? Justify using your answers and one other consideration.
questions.a: (a) 36 sq m. (b) 3078 + 150 = ₹3228. (c) ₹3230. (d) A costs ₹2 less (₹3228 against ₹3230) and buys only the area needed; B leaves 4 sq m spare that could be used elsewhere. Choose A for the lower bill, or B only if the spare carpet is useful.
s: Part (d): compares ₹3228 with ₹3230 and gives a reasoned choice using spare carpet

questions.q: Priya walks 0.725 km from her home to the bus stop and 0.725 km back each day, 6 days a week. (a) How far does she walk in one day? (b) How far in one week? (c) How far in 4 weeks? (d) Write the weekly distance in metres.
Which of these products, written in simplest decimal form (no final zero), has the fewest digits after the decimal point?
Meena says, "0.25 × 0.8 = 0.2, even though the rule says the product has 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places." Do you agree? Use the rule to explain.
questions.a: Yes. 25 × 8 = 200 and the product has 3 places, so it is 0.200, which equals 0.2. A zero at the end of the decimal part can be dropped without changing the value.
s: Gives the verdict that Meena is right
Applies the rule: 25 × 8 = 200 with 3 decimal places gives 0.200
Explains that the trailing zero does not change the value

questions.q: Amina buys 2.5 kg of ginger at ₹46.80 per kg and pays with a ₹200 note. The balance the shopkeeper returns is
True or False: Because 25 × 4 = 100, the product 2.5 × 0.4 equals 10.
questions.a: False. Each factor has one decimal digit, so the product has 1 + 1 = 2 decimal digits. The correct product is 1.00 = 1, not 10.
s: Counts 2 decimal digits in the product and gives 1.00 = 1

questions.q: A square tile has a side of 0.25 m. Meera needs 8 such tiles for a corner of her kitchen. The total area of the 8 tiles, in square metres, is
Hari walks 0.68 km from home to school and the same distance back, 5 days a week. How far does he walk in the week?
questions.a: 6.8 km

questions.q: (a) A lehenga needs 2.35 m of cloth. How much cloth do 4 lehengas need? (b) The cloth costs ₹180 per metre. What is the cost of the cloth for the 4 lehengas?
A stack of 40 identical coins has each coin 1.8 mm thick. Find the height of the stack in centimetres.
questions.a: Height = 1.8 × 40 = 72 mm = 7.2 cm.

questions.q:

Statement 1: 6.5 × 0.04 = 0.26.
Statement 2: 0.2 × 0.3 × 0.5 = 0.03.
Statement 3: 0.25 × 0.4, written in simplest form, has two digits after the decimal point.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q: A stationery shop in Indore buys 40 files at ₹18.75 each and sells all of them at ₹25 each. Find the cost, the sale amount and the profit.
questions.a: Cost = ₹750, sale = ₹1000, profit = ₹250.

Reason (R): The product of a decimal and a counting number can itself be a counting number.
questions.a: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.

s: First product checked, with two decimal factors
Second product checked, with a decimal and a counting number
Each has the correct number of decimal places

questions.q: Sana multiplies 0.19 × 0.36 and writes 0.684. Find her mistake and write the correct product.
questions.a: 19 × 36 = 684, but 0.19 has 2 places and 0.36 has 2 places, so the product needs 4 places, not 3: 0.0684.
s: Names the mistake: wrong number of decimal places (3 instead of 2 + 2 = 4)

questions.q: Write a decimal greater than 1 and a decimal between 0 and 1 whose product is (a) less than 1 and (b) greater than 1. Check each product.
questions.a: (a) 1.5 × 0.4 = 0.6, which is less than 1. (b) 4.5 × 0.8 = 3.6, which is greater than 1.
s: Pair for (a) with a correct product below 1
Pair for (b) with a correct product above 1
Both pairs fit one factor above 1 and one between 0 and 1

questions.q: Given 24 × 15 = 360, find (a) 2.4 × 1.5 (b) 0.24 × 0.15 (c) 24 × 0.15 (d) 0.024 × 1.5. (e) Which of these products are less than 1?
questions.a: (a) 3.6 (b) 0.036 (c) 3.6 (d) 0.036. (e) (b) and (d), since both equal 0.036; (a) and (c) are 3.6.
s: Parts (a) and (c): places the point to get 3.6 both times
Parts (b) and (d): places the point to get 0.036 both times

questions.q: Show that the product of 0.8 and any decimal between 0 and 1 cannot be 0.9.
questions.a: The product of two numbers between 0 and 1 is less than both. So it is less than 0.8. But 0.9 is more than 0.8, so 0.9 cannot be such a product.
s: States that both factors lie between 0 and 1
States the product is smaller than 0.8

questions.q: Dev has to find 48 × 0.97 and 48 × 1.03. (a) Without multiplying, say which of the two is greater than 48 and which is less, with the reason. (b) Find both products and say how far each one is from 48.
questions.a: (a) 48 × 1.03 is greater than 48 because 1.03 is more than 1; 48 × 0.97 is less than 48 because 0.97 is between 0 and 1. (b) 48 × 0.97 = 46.56 and 48 × 1.03 = 49.44; each is 1.44 away from 48.
s: Part (a): decides each comparison using whether the multiplier is below or above 1

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 7.5 × 0.96 is less than 7.5 and greater than 0.96.
Reason (R): 0.96 lies between 0 and 1 while 7.5 is greater than 1, so the product lies between the two numbers.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A school in Kochi has a notice board of 2.5 m by 1.6 m and wants to hang photo frames of 0.25 m by 0.16 m beside it. Painting costs ₹36.50 per square metre, and the office has ₹200 for painting the board and the frames. (a) Find the area of the board and the area of one frame. (b) Find the cost of painting the board and the cost of painting one frame. (c) Find the total cost of the board and 30 frames and the money left from ₹200. (d) The office must also keep ₹15 for varnish. Can it still paint 30 frames? If not, what is the largest number of frames it can paint? Show the cost.
questions.a: (a) Board 2.5 × 1.6 = 4 sq m; frame 0.25 × 0.16 = 0.04 sq m. (b) Board 4 × 36.50 = ₹146; one frame 0.04 × 36.50 = ₹1.46. (c) 30 frames cost 30 × 1.46 = ₹43.80; total ₹189.80; left ₹10.20. (d) No: only ₹185 is available and ₹189.80 is more than that. 26 frames cost ₹37.96, total ₹183.96, which is within ₹185; 27 frames cost ₹39.42, total ₹185.42, which is not. So at most 26 frames.
s: Part (a): areas 4 sq m and 0.04 sq m
Part (d): says 30 frames do not fit in ₹185 and shows 26 frames at ₹183.96 fit while 27 at ₹185.42 do not

questions.q: Manoj has 0.65 kg of rice. He gives 0.3 of it to a neighbour, and then 0.2 of what is left to a bird-feeding group. The rice in the bird-feeding group's share is

Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.a: The 0.6 m one has area below its side; the 1.4 m one has area above its side

questions.a: 0.81 times the original bill

questions.q: True or False: For every decimal x between 0 and 1, the product x × x × x is smaller than x × x.
questions.a: True. x × x × x is (x × x) multiplied by x, and x is between 0 and 1, so multiplying the positive number x × x by it gives something smaller (for example 0.9: 0.729 is less than 0.81).
s: Reason: multiplying x × x by x, which is between 0 and 1, reduces it, with an example

questions.q: Zoya says, "1.8 × 0.5 = 0.9 is smaller than both factors, because 0.5 is a decimal less than 1." Do you agree? Check using the product.
questions.a: No. 1.8 × 0.5 = 0.9. This is smaller than 1.8 but larger than 0.5, so it lies between the factors. The product is smaller than both factors only when both are between 0 and 1; here 1.8 is greater than 1.
s: Gives the verdict that Zoya is not right
Computes 0.9 and compares it with 0.5 and 1.8
Reason: one factor is above 1 so the product lies between them

questions.q: A sweet shop in Jaipur orders 2.5 kg of paneer at ₹320 per kg. The supplier offers two deals: Deal 1 charges 0.85 times the bill, and Deal 2 takes a flat ₹100 off the bill. (a) Find the bill before any deal. (b) Find the bill under Deal 1. (c) Is the Deal 1 bill more or less than the original bill, and why, without referring to the answer to (b)? (d) Which deal is better for this order? For what size of bill would the other deal be better? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) ₹800. (b) ₹680. (c) Less, because 0.85 lies between 0 and 1. (d) Deal 1 gives ₹680 against ₹700, so Deal 1 is better here. Deal 2 wins when 0.15 × bill is below 100, i.e. for bills under about ₹667.
s: Part (c): less, since 0.85 is between 0 and 1
Part (d): compares ₹680 with ₹700, picks Deal 1, and notes Deal 2 is better for bills under about ₹667

questions.q: (a) Find 0.75 × 0.4 and say whether it is smaller than both factors. (b) Give one pair of decimals whose product lies between the two factors, with the product.
questions.a: (a) 0.3, which is smaller than both 0.75 and 0.4. (b) For example 1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2, which lies between 0.8 and 1.5.
s: Part (a): product 0.3 and the comparison with both factors
Part (b): a valid pair, one factor above 1 and one below, with the correct product

questions.q: Ribbon costs ₹48 per metre. Sunita buys 1.25 m and Rekha buys 0.75 m. (a) Find each bill. (b) Say, without comparing digits, which bill is more than ₹48 and which is less, and why.
questions.a: (a) Sunita pays 48 × 1.25 = ₹60 and Rekha pays 48 × 0.75 = ₹36. (b) Sunita's is more than ₹48 because 1.25 is greater than 1; Rekha's is less because 0.75 is between 0 and 1.
s: Part (b): relates each bill to ₹48 through the multiplier compared with 1

questions.q:
Match each product in Column I with its value in Column II, using 63 × 14 = 882.
Column I: 1. 6.3 × 14  2. 0.63 × 0.14  3. 63 × 0.14  4. 630 × 1.4
Column II: a. 88.2  b. 0.0882  c. 8.82  d. 882
(a) Find 7 × 0.6 and say whether it is less than 1. (b) Without multiplying, say whether 0.07 × 0.06 is less than 1, with a reason.
questions.a: (a) 7 × 0.6 = 4.2, which is not less than 1. (b) Yes: both numbers are between 0 and 1, so the product is smaller than each of them, and each is less than 1 (the product is 0.0042).
s: Part (b): less than 1 because both factors are between 0 and 1

questions.q: Sort in increasing order, giving reasons that do not need the full multiplications: 56.4 × 0.83, 56.4 × 1.9, 56.4, 0.83, 1.9, 0.83 × 1.9.

questions.q: A dairy fills 42 litres of milk equally into 5 cans and sells 3 of the cans to a hotel. The milk sold to the hotel is
questions.a: 25.2 litres

questions.q: Imran says, "154 ÷ 4 = 38.5, so 0.154 ÷ 4 = 0.385 as well, because the digits are the same." Do you agree? Find the correct value.
questions.a: No. 0.154 is 154 divided by 1000, so 0.154 ÷ 4 = 38.5 ÷ 1000 = 0.0385. The digits are the same but the point moves three places left, not one.

questions.q: Rani divides 9.3 by 6 as follows: "9 ÷ 6 = 1 remainder 3. Put the point. Bring 3 tenths down to join the remainder 3, giving 6 tenths. 6 ÷ 6 = 1 tenth." So she writes 9.3 ÷ 6 = 1.1. (a) Find the step where she goes wrong. (b) Carry out the correct division, showing each remainder. (c) Check your quotient by multiplying by 6. (d) Show in one line that 1.1 cannot be the quotient.
questions.a: (a) The remainder 3 ones was joined to the 3 tenths as if it were 3 tenths; 3 ones is 30 tenths. (b) 9 ÷ 6 = 1 remainder 3 ones; 30 tenths + 3 tenths = 33 tenths; 33 ÷ 6 = 5 tenths remainder 3 tenths; 30 hundredths ÷ 6 = 5 hundredths, remainder 0; quotient 1.55. (c) 6 × 1.55 = 9.3. (d) 6 × 1.1 = 6.6, which is not 9.3.
s: Part (a): identifies that the remainder of 3 ones should have been regrouped as 30 tenths
Part (b): correct regrouping chain with remainders giving 1.55

questions.q: True or False: Since 45 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 1, we get 45 ÷ 4 = 11.1.
questions.a: False. The remainder 1 one is regrouped as 10 tenths, not 1 tenth: 10 tenths ÷ 4 = 2 tenths remainder 2 tenths, then 20 hundredths ÷ 4 = 5 hundredths. So 45 ÷ 4 = 11.25.
s: Corrects the regrouping (1 one is 10 tenths) and gives 11.25

questions.a: A leap year is divisible by 4. Two consecutive numbers differ by 1, so if one is a multiple of 4 the next leaves remainder 1 and cannot be one. So they cannot both be leap years.

questions.q: A press in Sivakasi prints a planner with one page for every day from 1 January 2096 to 31 December 2104, both included. questions.q: A science club in Nagpur compares three calendar rules over 400 years. Rule A adds a leap day every fourth year. Rule B is the rule used today (century years need divisibility by 400). Rule C adds a leap day every fourth year but never in a century year. The Earth needs 400 × 365.2422 days for 400 revolutions. (a) How many leap years do Rules A, B and C give in 400 years? (b) Find the days in 400 years under each rule. (c) Find how far each rule is from the Earth's days and whether it is ahead or behind. (d) A calendar maker must choose between Rule B and the simpler Rule C. After 1200 years (three such periods) how far off is each, and which would you choose?
questions.a: (a) A 100; B 97; C 96. (b) A 146100, B 146097, C 146096. (c) The Earth needs 146096.88. A is 3.12 days ahead, B is 0.12 days ahead, C is 0.88 days behind. (d) After 1200 years B is off by 3 × 0.12 = 0.36 days and C by 3 × 0.88 = 2.64 days. Rule C is easier to state, but its error grows more than seven times as fast, so Rule B is the better choice.
s: Part (c): differences 3.12 ahead, 0.12 ahead and 0.88 behind
Part (d): errors 0.36 and 2.64 days after 1200 years and a reasoned choice of Rule B
